headline: One new food a week is plenty
body:
Pick one new food.
Put a tiny bit on the plate.
No pressure to eat it.
caption:
Slow and steady is fine. One small new food a week adds up over months.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Looking counts as trying
body:
Seeing it on the plate counts.
Smelling it counts.
Touching it counts.
caption:
Every step toward a new food is progress, even if nothing gets eaten. Log the small steps so you can see them.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Safe foods are a tool
body:
Write down what they reliably eat.
Build meals around it.
Add one new thing at a time.
caption:
A safe-foods list isn't a failure. It's your starting point for calmer meals.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Serve one safe food every meal
body:
Always include one familiar food.
Put the new food beside it.
Mealtime feels less risky.
caption:
A familiar food on the plate keeps mealtimes calm while a new one shows up.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Make the new food tiny
body:
One pea-sized piece.
One small bite on the side.
Nothing to finish.
caption:
A small amount feels less scary than a full serving.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: The 5-minute mealtime reset
body:
Sit together.
Phones away.
Turn the mood down, not up.
caption:
If dinner is tense, reset the mood first. Calm tables make trying new things easier.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Skip the bribes
body:
No dessert deals.
No bargaining bites.
Just offer it again another day.
caption:
Bribes can make a food feel like a chore. Keep it neutral and offer again.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Praise the step, not the bite
body:
"You smelled it, nice!"
"You touched it!"
"Thanks for trying."
caption:
Celebrate effort. Skip pressure.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: 10-minute Sunday meal plan
body:
List safe foods.
Pick meals for the week.
Add one try-it food.
caption:
A short plan on Sunday saves a lot of stress on Wednesday.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Lunchbox formula
body:
1 familiar food.
1 easy-to-try food.
1 fun extra.
caption:
A simple formula makes packing a lunchbox faster. Save this for back-to-school week.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Dips make new foods easier
body:
Ranch.
Hummus.
Yogurt dip.
caption:
A familiar dip can make a new food feel less strange. Keep the dip on the side.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Offer a choice of two
body:
Do you want carrots or cucumber?
Both are fine.
They pick.
caption:
Choosing between two options gives kids a sense of control without a standoff.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Let them help in the kitchen
body:
Washing veggies.
Stirring.
Picking the plate.
caption:
Kids who touch and handle food are often more curious about it.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Separate sections, same plate
body:
Keep foods apart.
No mixed-up sauces.
Let them choose the order.
caption:
Some kids like foods not touching. A divided plate keeps meals easy.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: What counts in a try-it log?
body:
Saw it. Touched it. Smelled it.
Licked it. Tried a bite.
Ate some.
caption:
Each step is a small win. A try-it tracker helps you notice them.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Change the shape
body:
Cut sandwiches into stars.
Curl cucumber strips.
Use a cutter.
caption:
A new shape can make a familiar food feel fun.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Fun cutters for lunchboxes
body:
Cheese stars.
Melon hearts.
Sandwich dinosaurs.
caption:
Cheap cutters make lunchbox packing a little more fun.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Make snack time predictable
body:
Same time each day.
Same spot.
Same calm routine.
caption:
Predictable routines make mealtimes feel safer.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Retire "clean your plate"
body:
Say "listen to your body."
Leave room to stop.
No plate-cleaning rules.
caption:
Staying neutral keeps meals low pressure.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Keep meals around 20 minutes
body:
Set a timer.
After it ends, we're done.
Offer again next meal.
caption:
A clear end keeps meals calm for everyone.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Plan the grocery list around safe foods
body:
Check your safe-foods list.
Buy what you need.
Add one new food to try.
caption:
Shopping from a list avoids wasted food and last-minute stress.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Eat together when you can
body:
Same table.
Same foods when possible.
Let them watch you eat.
caption:
Seeing parents enjoy food can make new foods feel normal.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Screens off at the table
body:
Phones away.
TV off.
Talk about the day.
caption:
Fewer distractions make it easier to notice what food looks and tastes like.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Talk about textures
body:
Crunchy. Soft. Smooth.
Salty. Sweet.
Skip "yummy" and "yucky."
caption:
Describing food neutrally makes it less loaded.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: School lunch? Keep it familiar
body:
Pack safe foods.
Add one tiny new thing.
Don't expect a miracle.
caption:
Lunch is not the place for big experiments. Save those for home.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Visiting grandparents?
body:
Share your safe-foods list.
Send a few staples.
Keep expectations low.
caption:
A short list helps relatives feed your child with less stress.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Log the small wins
body:
Tried a bite.
Asked for more.
Sat at the table.
caption:
A quick weekly note shows progress that is easy to miss.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: When to talk to your pediatrician
body:
Very few foods eaten.
Weight loss or gagging.
Meals cause real distress.
caption:
These are signs to check in with your pediatrician or a feeding specialist. A planner can't replace professional help.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Start here: calmer mealtimes
body:
1. List safe foods.
2. Plan the week.
3. Log tiny steps.
caption:
New here? Those three steps are the whole system. Follow along for a tip every day.

Link in bio for the planner.

headline: Friday 2-minute wins check
body:
What worked this week?
What did not?
What will you try next?
caption:
Two minutes on Friday shows you what is working. Small notes beat big plans.
